description: Same physical FireSim bitstream as chipyard_gemmini_opu_hetero.json (alveo_u250_firesim_shuttle_gemmini_opu) but the runtime treats hart 1 as PLAIN RVV (no Saturn OPU custom instructions). Saturn OPU IS RVV base + OP-V extensions, so plain RVV kernels execute on the OPU unit correctly. Picks kernels from kernels/gemmini/ + kernels/rvv/ instead of kernels/gemmini/ + kernels/rvv_opu/. Both sets are bit_exact-equivalent vs the Q0.31 PyTorch golden (gemmini does software Q0.31 requantize in im2col_full_C; rvv kernels use the same Q0.31 fixed-point requantize tail), so the cross-backend drift constraint (requantize_ops: [conv2d_s8, linear_s8]) is unnecessary — conv/linear can run on either tile freely. This matches the kernel pair (rvv + gemmini_q31) that Dima used for the qrb5165 image.

cores.name: gemmini0
cores.description: Shuttle scalar + Gemmini int8 RoCC. Curated im2col_full_C kernel does software Q0.31 requantize — bit-exact vs PyTorch Q0.31 golden (max_abs_err=0 validated on Saturn FireSim May 2026).

cores.name: rvv0
cores.description: Shuttle + Saturn OPU vector unit, but kernels here use ONLY base RVV instructions (no OP-V customs). Curated rvv_conv2d_s8 / rvv_linear_s8 / rvv_silu_s8 do the Q0.31 fixed-point requantize tail bit-exact-equivalent to the gemmini im2col_full_C path.

notes: Runs on the existing GemminiAndOPUShuttleConfig FireSim bitstream — no rebuild needed. The OPU custom instructions are unused (kernels never emit VOPACC/OPMVINBCAST/etc.) but the Shuttle hart still decodes plain RVV via the OPU unit's base RVV implementation.

Replaces the requantize_ops drift constraint we needed with rvv_opu kernels (which were tagged NUMERIC_DRIFT). With both backends doing software Q0.31 requantize, the scheduler can split conv2d_s8 / linear_s8 across tiles freely — the regime that gives qrb its tight 75.71 ms schedule.
